title: Senior Project Manager Salary: How to Calculate Your Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate
description: Learn how to convert a senior project manager salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks, plus tax, Medicare, and superannuation estimates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: Using the ABS average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, a senior project manager working 38 hours earns about $108,352 annually before tax, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical senior project manager salary range in Australia?
faqs.a: Senior project manager salaries vary widely by industry, location, and experience. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to roughly $108,350 per year for a 38-hour week. Many senior project managers earn above this average, often between $120,000 and $160,000, but award minimums may apply under awards such as the Professional Employees Award. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides to check award-specific rates.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $54.31 per hour × 38 × 52 = $108,352 per year. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The calculator on this site does this for you, and you can add casual loading if applicable.

faqs.q: Does superannuation count as part of my senior project manager salary?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your base salary. Under the Super Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830) into a super fund. For a $108,352 annual salary, that's an extra $13,002 in super, but it is not included in your take-home pay. The calculator on this site shows super separately.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the senior project manager salary calculation

If you are a senior project manager negotiating a new role or reviewing an offer, you may see a rate expressed as an hourly figure, a weekly wage, or an annual salary. Converting between these formats helps you compare offers and understand your total remuneration. The standard approach is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For full-time employees, the typical assumption is 38 hours per week, as set by the National Employment Standards.

For example, if you earn $60 per hour and work 38 hours each week, your annual gross salary is $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560. This figure does not include superannuation, which your employer pays on top. The same calculation works for any hourly rate, whether you are on an award, an enterprise agreement, or an individual contract.

### Why 38 hours is the standard

The Fair Work Ombudsman defines the National Minimum Wage as $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, which equals $1,004.90 per week. This 38-hour week is the benchmark for full-time employment in most awards. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust the weekly hours in the formula. Part-time and casual employees should use their actual weekly hours.

### Fortnightly pay is common

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the example above, $60 per hour × 38 hours = $2,280 per week, so your fortnightly gross is $4,560. The calculator on this site shows both weekly and fortnightly amounts.

## Award rates and the National Minimum Wage

Senior project managers may be covered by an award such as the Professional Employees Award or the Managers and Professionals Award. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides that list the minimum hourly rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each classification. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%, and the National Minimum Wage rose to $26.44 per hour. However, most senior project managers earn well above the minimum. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $54.31 per hour for a 38-hour week. This is a useful benchmark, but your actual rate depends on your industry, experience, and location.

### Casual loading and superannuation

If you work as a casual senior project manager, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% casual loading. For example, if the base award rate is $40 per hour, the casual rate would be $50 per hour. The calculator on this site has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate – do not enter a rate that already includes loading. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $118,560 annual salary, that’s an extra $14,227 in super, but it is not part of your take-home pay.

## Tax and Medicare on your annual figure

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax and Medicare levy using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, though low-income earners may pay a reduced rate or nil. For a senior project manager earning $118,560, the tax would be approximately $28,867 plus Medicare of $2,371, leaving a take-home pay of about $87,322 per year. These are estimates only – your actual tax may vary due to deductions, offsets, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

### Using the timesheet calculator

To quickly convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super estimates, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. Enter your base hourly rate, check the casual loading box if you are casual, and the calculator will show your gross annual salary, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. You can also refer to [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to check award-specific minimums. For a deeper dive into tax brackets, see [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) or [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Important disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Senior project manager salary in context

While the National Minimum Wage provides a floor, senior project managers typically command rates far above that. The ABS average full-time earnings give a ballpark of around $108,000 to $110,000 per year, but many senior roles in construction, IT, or engineering exceed $150,000. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for minimum entitlements, and use the [reference tables](/data) on this site to compare rates across industries. Remember that your total package includes super, which is paid on top, so a $120,000 salary plus 12% super gives a total remuneration of $134,400.

### Final tips

- Always clarify whether a quoted rate includes casual loading or super.
- Use the calculator on [the timesheet](/) to see your fortnightly and annual figures.
- Consult the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool for award-specific rates.
- For tax planning, refer to the Australian Taxation Office’s individual tax rates.

By understanding how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay, you can confidently compare job offers and negotiate your senior project manager salary.
